reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it chiefly walks beginners through Binance Earn features, explaining how staking and other rewards work while discussing lockups, changing rates, and investment risks. The creator includes a Binance referral link and describes how to subscribe or stake, but the video does not establish a deceptive promise or a fraudulent money or data flow.

They're pretty basic. They are for beginners in crypto, but I feel like there are a lot of beginners in crypto and I want them to have a safe place where they can watch tutorials and get everything explained to them.
while you're holding your crypto or stable coins then of course you can earn passive rewards on that
All we do, we click subscribe.
Be aware that, usually if you can get a higher rate, there are other risks involved!

opening.argument: The presentation links passive returns directly to placing assets into Binance products and taking the required participation step. It says viewers can earn rewards while holding crypto or stablecoins, identifies Binance Earn as the place for those features, and then instructs them to click subscribe. The relationship is therefore not merely educational: transfer or commitment of crypto is paired with an income claim. The on-screen product list reinforces that pairing by displaying APR percentages beside flexible or time-based options and subscription controls. The description also sends viewers to exchange registration links while advertising sign-up bonuses, showing a broader pattern of directing viewers toward financial participation. Taken together, the content presents staking and related products as a practical route to passive income, which fits an investment-pool or staking-return solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a guide does not remove the participation pathway. The cited explanation is immediately operational: viewers are shown where to find Earn and told to subscribe, while the product screens display returns beside the action controls. The disclaimer that it is not financial advice does not establish that the advertised return relationship is reliable or adequately qualified. Nor does mentioning risks eliminate the central solicitation to place crypto into yield products.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The material explains how products work and repeatedly identifies material risks rather than promising a guaranteed return. It says rates vary, lockups differ, and higher rates carry other risks. It also explains that liquidity farming has not been successful for the speaker and that asset prices can fall faster than the earned percentage. Those qualifications undermine the claim that the video presents a deceptive fixed-return scheme.

opening.argument: The combination of unusually high displayed returns, crypto staking, and direct action controls creates a meaningful red-flag pattern. The spoken discussion mentions liquidity-farming APRs reaching 300% or 500%, while the sampled Binance screens visibly pair substantial APR figures with Subscribe controls and selected durations. The description simultaneously advertises a $30,000 sign-up bonus and a $1,000 sign-up bonus through external exchange links. Even if individual figures have conditions, the overall presentation makes asset participation appear capable of producing exceptional or passive rewards. The video also frames these products as accessible to beginners, increasing the concern that attention-grabbing rates and bonuses may drive inexperienced viewers toward financial commitments before they can evaluate the underlying conditions.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of risk language does not neutralize the visual and verbal emphasis on returns. The audience sees percentages and action buttons in the product interface, and hears that returns can reach 300% or 500%. External bonus links add another inducement. A disclaimer is not evidence that viewers receive clear, proportionate treatment of eligibility, sustainability, or loss conditions; it simply shifts responsibility while the promotional signals remain prominent.

The speaker warns that higher rates involve other risks and explains that liquidity farming can miss gains when token values change. The sampled screens show product interfaces, but they do not establish that any viewer received a promised payout or that the displayed rates were unconditional.

opening.argument: Although the speaker adopts a beginner-tutorial role, the content functions as promotion because it repeatedly walks viewers toward Binance earning products and supplies a referral pathway. The video explains that viewers can stake, subscribe, redeem, and obtain rewards, while the description provides a Binance registration link and states that the creator receives a percentage of trading fees. That financial connection matters: the presenter is not a detached reviewer describing an unrelated service, but someone directing viewers to a platform from which he may benefit. The tutorial framing can make the solicitation appear safer and more neutral than it is, especially when the subject is passive income and the audience is explicitly described as crypto beginners.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive: it demonstrates the path from holding assets to staking and rewards, then directs viewers to a referral link. Saying the creator receives only a small percentage does not make the financial incentive disappear. The question is whether the tutorial steers participation while presenting passive income as accessible, and the combination of beginner targeting, operational instructions, and referral compensation supports that reading.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The referral relationship is openly disclosed, which supports ordinary promotion rather than concealment. The speaker does not merely tout returns: he explains changing APRs, lockups, redemption timing, token-price exposure, and the inability to withdraw some staked funds immediately. He also says liquidity farming was unsuccessful for him. Those details are consistent with an operational tutorial containing cautions, not proof that the educational framing masks fraud.
